implementation.summary: D32 adds a real two-partition streaming campaign and fixes checkpoint partition expansion. The live fixture produces 12 records across partitions 0 and 1, drains six bounded micro-batches of two records, verifies per-partition lag 6/6 to 0/0, and retains the existing poison, oversized-record and recovery assertions. The candidate also carries the corrected capability-progress consistency test.

security_and_recovery.live_provider: The live runner started an isolated real Redpanda broker and Ronin API, seeded a two-partition topic, ran Chromium against the Streaming Studio journey, correlated every API event to structured logs and removed the isolated container/network.
security_and_recovery.negative_paths: The journey retains invalid/poison/oversized input WARN assertions and checks that failed poison processing does not advance lag; partitioned polling also checks bounded idle retries and unchanged lag. The capability progress test rejects a false zero-progress claim while requiring release_ready=false.
security_and_recovery.provider_scope: Redpanda/Kafka was exercised as a real local provider. PostgreSQL and the worker were not started in this streaming-only campaign; no external broker or full provider matrix is claimed.
security_and_recovery.recovery_scope: The campaign proves bounded multi-partition drain, checkpoint expansion and final zero lag. It does not establish continuous operation, broker/process failure recovery, backpressure exhaustion, operator rollback or complete P11 qualification.
